key_insight: Evidence-Backed Video QA asks models to answer questions and provide precise temporal and pixel-level evidence, revealing that strong QA accuracy does not necessarily mean true visual understanding.
engineering_relevance: The paper provides a practical pathway to more trustworthy video AI by pairing large video-language models with grounded evidence generation and evaluation for explainable, verifiable outputs.
method: Define E-VQA with joint outputs: semantic answer + temporal segments + tracked dense segmentation masklets.
Introduce ST-Evidence, a human-verified benchmark for discriminative and generative pixel-level grounding.
Build ST-Evidence-Instruct, a 160k-scale automated training set for fine-tuning grounded Video LLMs.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a clear QA–perception gap in state-of-the-art models and shows that fine-tuning on ST-Evidence-Instruct improves grounding substantially, including +27.2 t-mean and +13.8 J&F on a 7B model.
watch_item: The automated evidence-generation pipeline may be sensitive to grounding noise or tracking errors, so deployment should verify evidence quality beyond answer accuracy.
